question: Which one of the following is true about the Range and Interquartile Range of a given data?
options: A. Both are affected by extreme values in the data.
B. Both are measures of the variability of each item in the data.
C. Both are considering only the middle 50% of the data.
D. Both are measures of variation of the data.
explanation:
The Range and Interquartile Range (IQR) are both measures of variation because they describe the spread of data.

 Range considers the full spread (max - min), while IQR considers the spread of the middle 50%.

 Therefore, both are measures of variation, but only the Range is affected by extreme values.

question: Which one of the following is a simple random sampling?
options: A. Selecting five students from Grade 12 students of the same school randomly.
B. Selecting a group randomly from groups formed by dividing the population into groups.
C. First the population is divided into homogenous groups and a sample is selected from each homogenous group.
D. First divide a city into ten groups and choose the secondary school principals from the randomly selected 3 groups.
explanation:
Simple random sampling is when every member of the population has an equal chance of being selected. 

Option A randomly selects five students from all Grade 12 students, giving each student an equal chance. 

Other options involve grouping or stratifying, which are different sampling methods.
